sections.normalized_html: If the path [MATH: C] is the line segment [MATH: \overline{AB}] traversed from the point [MATH: A(0,0)] to the point [MATH: B(1, 1),] calculate the line integral [MATH: \displaystyle \int\limits_C x^2y\,\mathrm{d}x + xy\,\mathrm{d}y.]
sections.readable_text:
If the path [MATH: C] is the line segment [MATH: \overline{AB}] traversed from the point [MATH: A(0,0)] to the point [MATH: B(1, 1),] calculate the line integral
[MATH: \displaystyle \int\limits_C x^2y\,\mathrm{d}x + xy\,\mathrm{d}y.]

sections.normalized_html:
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are [MATH: \mathbf{a} = 0\,\mathbf{i} + 0\,\mathbf{j}] and [MATH: \mathbf{b} = 1\,\mathbf{i} + 1\,\mathbf{j}.] So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by [MATH: r(t)|= a + t(b − a); = ti + tj,]

where [MATH: 0 \le t \le 1.] So, we have that [MATH: x(t) = t] and [MATH: y(t) = t] along the segment.

The derivative of [MATH: \mathbf r(t)] is given by [MATH: r^{′}(t)|= (dx)/(dt)i + (dy)/(dt)j = i + j.]

We can now evaluate the line integral: [MATH: ∫_(C)x^{2}ydx + xydy|= ∫_{0}^{1}x^{2}y(dx)/(dt)dt + xy(dy)/(dt)dt; = ∫_{0}^{1}(x^{2}y(dx)/(dt) + xy(dy)/(dt))dt; = ∫_{0}^{1}t^{2} ⋅ t ⋅ 1 + t ⋅ t ⋅ 1dt; = ∫_{0}^{1}t^{3} + t^{2}dt; = [(t^{4})/(4) + (t^{3})/(3)]_{0}^{1}; = (1)/(4) + (1)/(3); = (7)/(12)]

sections.readable_text:
If the path [MATH: C] is a part of the parabola [MATH: y=x^2] traversed from the point [MATH: A(0,0)] to the point [MATH: B(1,1),] evaluate the line integral
[MATH: \displaystyle \int\limits_C (x+y)\,\mathrm{d}x + (x-y)\,\mathrm{d}y.]

sections.normalized_html:
Notice that our curve is given by the explicit Cartesian equation [MATH: y = x^2.] As a result, we obtain the following parametrization of the curve: [MATH: r(t) = x(t)i + y(t)j = ti + t^{2}j, t ∈ [0, 1]]

The derivative of [MATH: \mathbf r(t)] is given by [MATH: r^{′}(t)|= (dx)/(dt)i + (dy)/(dt)j = i + 2tj.]

We can now evaluate the line integral:

[MATH: ∫_(C)(x + y)dx + (x − y)dy|= ∫_{0}^{1}(x + y)(dx)/(dt)dt + (x − y)(dy)/(dt)dt; = ∫_{0}^{1}((x + y)(dx)/(dt) + (x − y)(dy)/(dt))dt; = ∫_{0}^{1}(t + t^{2}) ⋅ 1 + (t − t^{2}) ⋅ 2tdt; = ∫_{0}^{1}t + 3t^{2} − 2t^{3}dt; = [(t^{2})/(2) + t^{3} − (t^{4})/(2)]_{0}^{1}; = [(1)/(2) + 1 − (1)/(2)] − [0]; = 1]
